question: Which seed-syllable, endowed with life and vital breath, must be uttered in this practice?
premises: The vāgbhava seed-syllable is specified as the object of utterance.
This seed-syllable is designated as something to be uttered.
The utterance must be accompanied by life and vital breath.
inference: Therefore, the practitioner must utter the vāgbhava bīja while it is conjoined with jīva and prāṇa.
uncertainties: The precise technical sense of jīva and prāṇa in this Śrīvidyā context (literal breath, subtle vital forces, or mantra-internal features) is not fully specified in this verse alone.
plain_english: One should utter the vāgbhava seed-syllable, endowed with life and vital breath.
